findings.title: USE failure now permanently drains the node's connection pool
findings.claim: A USE that keeps failing causes every new connection to be dropped and the pool to drain to Broken(UseKeyspaceError), firing a Lost event for a still-reachable node, whereas the base only warned and kept the connection.

findings.title: USE-failure log downgraded from warn! to debug! despite worse outcome
findings.claim: The failure log level was lowered from warn! to debug!, and the error only reaches last_error when the pool is not filling and is empty, so repeated keyspace failures are invisible at default log levels while the pool isn't empty.

findings.title: Keyspace-failure log uses {} formatting unlike sibling arms' {:?}
findings.claim: The new log arm formats the error with {} while the sibling arms use {:?}, an inconsistency in formatting specifiers.

findings.title: Comment claims failed connection re-enters pool logic, but it's now dropped
findings.claim: The comment says the connection 'will travel through this logic again, to be finally put into the conns,' but on a failed USE the connection is now dropped, making the comment stale.

findings.title: Missing timeout on per-connection USE now also blocks the empty-pool error path
findings.claim: The pre-existing TODO that there should be a timeout now matters more: a hanging USE keeps ready_connections non-empty, which blocks both refill scheduling and the new empty-pool error publication that depends on is_filling() being false.

findings.title: New error variant text overstates when the keyspace failure occurs
findings.claim: The message 'Failed to set keyspace while initializing a connection' overstates the step, since the only producer runs after OPTIONS/STARTUP and also after later keyspace changes, not just during initialization.

findings.title: #[from] on new variant lets ? silently convert a recoverable error
findings.claim: The #[from] attribute adds a public From<UseKeyspaceError> for ConnectionError, so a ? could silently turn a recoverable Session::use_keyspace error into a type documented as meaning the connection is unusable.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill test never calls run()
findings.claim: The test checks need_filling() and the error flag but never calls run(), so it doesn't actually show a refill gets scheduled or that backoff grows.

findings.title: Test fixture uses RequestTimeout variant that this code path can't produce
findings.claim: The test's fixture uses UseKeyspaceError::RequestTimeout, but this path cannot produce that because the per-connection USE has no timeout.

findings.title: No test for keyspace failure while pool is empty with attempts in flight
findings.claim: There is no test covering a keyspace failure occurring while the pool is empty but other connection attempts are still in flight.

findings.title: No test asserts the Lost event fires on keyspace failure
findings.claim: No test covers the Lost connectivity event on keyspace failure; existing tests pass None as the sender.

findings.title: No test for resharding with non-empty excess_connections
findings.claim: There is no test covering resharding when excess_connections is non-empty.

findings.title: Test waits via 1ms polling loop instead of a deterministic notification
findings.claim: The 1ms polling loop with a 5s bound works but isn't deterministic since no existing notification covers the excess-clear branch in run(); extracting the event-handling logic into its own method would let the test call it directly instead of polling.

findings.title: Redundant assert after worker.await repeats the loop condition
findings.claim: The assert placed after worker.await simply repeats the condition already checked by the polling loop.

findings.title: PR body references issue #1682 which does not exist in the repo
findings.claim: gh api repos/dkropachev/quillstone/issues/1682 returns 404, so the 'Fixes: #1682' reference in the PR body points to a nonexistent issue and needs a repo qualifier or removal per CONTRIBUTING.md.

findings.title: Validation run omits --features metrics, leaving metrics tests unrun
findings.claim: The cited cargo test run for keyspace_setup_failure doesn't pass --features metrics, so the three #[cfg(feature = "metrics")] tests and the metric asserts inside both keyspace tests were never compiled or run.

findings.title: Metric-balancing fix committed without its test in a separate commit
findings.claim: de164845 changes metric balancing with no test, and the test arrives separately in 0d91aa54, against the 'one logically coherent change per commit' and 'bug fixes are covered with tests' conventions.

findings.title: Fixup commit should be squashed into the commit that added the test
findings.claim: 617139df only rewrites a wait inside a test added earlier in the same PR and should be squashed into 0d91aa54.

findings.title: All four commit messages are subject-only with no body
findings.claim: None of the four commits has a message body explaining what changes and why, as CONTRIBUTING.md asks.

findings.title: New error message wording breaks the pattern used by existing variants
findings.claim: The new message 'Failed to set keyspace while initializing a connection: {0}' differs from the existing three variants' "'USE KEYSPACE <>' request failed: {0}" wording, and from neighbouring connection-error variants that are #[error(transparent)].

findings.title: New keyspace tests skip setup_tracing() used by every nearby test
findings.claim: The new tests at :1474 and :1526 skip calling setup_tracing(), which every nearby test calls.

findings.title: New keyspace tests build PoolRefiller by hand instead of using helper
findings.claim: The new tests construct PoolRefiller::new(...) manually instead of using the existing mock_pool_refiller() helper.

findings.title: New keyspace tests re-implement Options/Startup rules already provided
findings.claim: The new tests rebuild the Options/Startup rules that start_simulated_node already provides.

findings.title: decrement_total_connections loops one atomic op per connection instead of batching
findings.claim: decrement_total_connections runs one atomic dec_total_connections() call per connection; a sub_total_connections(n) (plus a no-op twin) would do it in a single operation.

findings.title: Test loops incrementing counters per connection are fine as written
findings.claim: The report notes the test loops at :1957 and :1984 are fine since each increment mirrors one real open, i.e. no change needed there.

findings.title: Empty-pool check condition duplicated between two code locations
findings.claim: The condition 'if !self.is_filling() && self.is_empty() { update_shared_conns(..) }' is repeated between :895-897 and :908-910; a small helper would keep the two branches in step.

findings.title: Keyspace failure represented by two error types that must stay in sync
findings.claim: Keyspace failure is now represented by both the private ConnectionSetupError::Keyspace and the public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError; if one changes without the other, they disagree.

findings.title: New test helper nearly duplicates an existing one, differing by one field
findings.claim: unrequested_connection_event nearly duplicates shard_aware_attempt_result, differing only in requested_shard; one helper taking Option<RequestedShard> would cover both, and the current name doesn't explain why it's separate.

findings.title: PR description doesn't mention the pool can now permanently drain
findings.claim: The PR says the pool 'schedules another refill' but doesn't describe that when the failure is independent of the connection (e.g. a dropped keyspace), every refill fails and the node's pool eventually breaks where the base kept serving with a warning.

findings.title: PR description covers only one of the four commits' changes
findings.claim: Three commits (de164845, 0d91aa54, 617139df) balance total_connections at three points (full-pool excess clear, excess-limit clear, and resharding), but the PR body never mentions these changes or their motivation.

findings.title: Refiller keeps stale sharder/shard-aware-port while USE keeps failing
findings.claim: The sharder and shard-aware-port updates now wait until USE succeeds, so while USE keeps failing the refiller keeps the old sharder/shard_aware_port and keeps targeting the old shard layout.

findings.title: No new waits, cancellation points, or timeouts added on public calls
findings.claim: Compared to base, the PR adds no new waits, cancellation points, or timeouts on public calls; Session::use_keyspace keeps its connect_timeout.

findings.title: Validation filter accurately matches the two cited passing tests
findings.claim: The validation filter matches exactly the two tests at :1474 and :1526, so the claim of '2 passed' is accurate.
